First, we expand the parentheses and use the Pythagorean identity.

$$
\begin{aligned}\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,{(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{8})+\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{8}))}^{2} & ={sin}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{8})+2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{8})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{8})+{cos}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{8}) \\  & =[{sin}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{8})+{cos}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{8})]+2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{8})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{8}) \\  & =1+2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{8})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{8})\end{aligned}
$$

Let's recall the double-angle formula for sine:

$$
2\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x=\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)
$$

Substituting $x=\frac{\pi }{8}$ into the above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{8})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{8}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{8}) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we obtain

$$
1+2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{8})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{8})=1+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}.
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
{(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{8})+\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{8}))}^{2}=1+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}.
$$
